text: R2: WHEN a legal entity is retired, the system SHALL exclude it from selection for new business.

comments.text: R2 (and its criterion A4, "WHEN a retired legal entity is offered as a choice for a new reference, the system SHALL not offer it") cannot be exercised by anything in this spec: the Scope explicitly puts "links from trades, agreements or collateral to a legal entity" OUT, and the register itself has no ref fields, so there is no picker in these artifacts that could offer a retired entity. As written, A4 has no test surface in this document. Either restate R2 as an invariant the register guarantees to consumers (e.g. the entity exposes an 'active-or-draft only' selection view that consuming specs pick over), or mark R2 as verifiable only once a consuming spec exists and say so.

text: Records carry a draft/active/retired lifecycle so a retired entity can be kept for history without being selectable for new business.

comments.text: The lifecycle is declared but no requirement governs its transitions: nothing states how a record moves from draft to active, whether active can go back to draft, whether retired can be reactivated, or whether a draft (not yet active) entity is selectable for new business — R2 only excludes retired. Since the status field and its default(draft) are the spec's own addition beyond CDM, the transition rules are this spec's substance to define; without them, implementers and the A-criteria for lifecycle behaviour have nothing to test against.

text: R1: WHEN a legal entity is retired, the system SHALL keep the record and its identifiers unchanged and available for history.

comments.text: "Keep ... unchanged" is ambiguous between two different behaviours: (a) retirement must not delete or alter data (which is what A3 actually tests), or (b) a retired record becomes immutable and can no longer be edited. If (b) is intended, that is an additional, currently missing requirement with its own criterion; if (a) is intended, consider wording R1 as 'shall not delete or modify the record' so it cannot be read as an edit lock.

text: The system SHALL keep at most one identifier of type LEI across the whole register — two legal entities never share an LEI, and one entity never carries two.

comments.text: P1 constrains the Data model (it names a bean, a field or a choice value), but the Data model's 'Rules the table cannot carry' list does not cite it. Add an P1 entry there, or say why it is omitted, so the two sections agree on which rules live outside the table.

text: The system SHALL accept a LEI-typed identifier only when its value is 20 alphanumeric characters (ISO 17442). [ASSUMED: the format applies only to identifiers whose type is LEI.]

comments.text: P2 constrains the Data model (it names a bean, a field or a choice value), but the Data model's 'Rules the table cannot carry' list does not cite it. Add an P2 entry there, or say why it is omitted, so the two sections agree on which rules live outside the table.

text: On the edit form, the identifier list should read as a simple add/remove list of rows (type + value), with the LEI row visibly marked so the 20-character rule is discoverable.

comments.text: This behaviour lives only as prose in the User interface section — no requirement states it and no acceptance criterion verifies it, so nothing in the document can fail if the edit form renders the identifier list differently. Either promote it to a requirement (e.g. the edit form presents identifiers as an add/remove list and visibly marks LEI rows) with a criterion, or mark it explicitly as non-normative guidance so a reviewer knows it is not acceptance-tested.

text: each record carries a required name and optional identifiers (LEI, BIC, MIC, RED ID, country cod e, other)

comments.text: The Intent lists six identifier types, but the type vocabulary is CDM's EntityIdentifierTypeEnum (listed under Dependencies). Can you confirm that enum actually contains members for 'country code' and 'other'? If it does not, the Data model's embedded EntityIdentifier either cannot express those types or needs a type source beyond the CDM enum — worth settling now, since P2's scope ('applies only to identifiers whose type is LEI') and A2's BIC/other clause both lean on the type set being well-defined.
